beats.text: Every single time Cursor or Claude writes code for you, your GPU wastes up to 70% of its compute doing nothing.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a clean code editor on the left and a robot arm failing to grasp a cup on the right.

beats.text: The bottleneck is a perception-action disconnect; agents treat the world like a static string, ignoring the chaotic, fluid dynamics of real-time spatial physics.
beats.visual_focus: A 3D wireframe of a robot arm attempting to grasp a moving object, with red error vectors showing missed spatial coordinates.

beats.text: Enter RobotWorld: a rigorous simulation testbed that forces agents to prove their spatial reasoning across 84 complex manipulation and locomotion tasks.
beats.visual_focus: A high-speed radar plot expanding to show 84 distinct task nodes being mapped in real-time.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—it hit that 'AI is smart but useless' pain point immediately. I liked that you didn't use any 'smart drawer' metaphors. However, 'execution trace analysis' sounds a bit like a buzzword salad unless you actually show a snippet of the log or the visual overlay. I'm curious about the 'perception-action disconnect'—if you had shown a 1-second clip of a robot failing a grasp, it would have been a 10/10.
